correctness.rationale: Independent reduction gives trace \((2+\sigma-2r)/(1+\sigma)\), determinant \((1-r)/(1+\sigma)\), and discriminant \((\sigma^2-4r(1-r))/(1+\sigma)^2\). Below the repeated-root threshold the eigenvalues are conjugate with modulus \(\sqrt{(1-r)/(1+\sigma)}\), strictly decreasing. Above it the larger real root has positive derivative. Hence the unique minimum is at \(\sigma_*=2\sqrt{r(1-r)}\). Substitution into \(r=\sigma^2a^2/\beta\) gives the beta formula. Independent numerical monotonicity checks covered representative \(r\) values from 0.05 to 0.95.

value.rationale: The formula gives an exact calibration of a free primal/dual ratio on the canonical one-singular-value model, and identifies the same underdamped/overdamped transition that later adaptive spectral methods try to locate numerically. It is a useful analytic benchmark rather than an arbitrary parameter sample.
residual_risks: A later or differently phrased scalar specialization of Fercoq's general spectral-radius framework could record the same closed form.

final_claim: For scalar least-squares PDHG/PDAL with fixed modal product \(r=\tau\sigma a^2\in(0,1)\), the spectral radius is uniquely minimized at \(\sigma_*=2\sqrt{r(1-r)}\), equivalently \(\beta_*=4a^2(1-r)\), with minimum \(\sqrt{1-r}/(\sqrt r+\sqrt{1-r})\); the optimum is the repeated-root boundary.
limitations: A matrix problem with several singular values becomes a shared-ratio minimax problem and is not covered.
A later or differently phrased scalar specialization of Fercoq's general spectral-radius framework could record the same closed form.
